review.title: Tidelands near cities withheld from sale
review.plain: Tidelands within two miles of any incorporated city, city and county, or town and fronting on navigable harbors, estuaries, bays or inlets shall be withheld from grant or sale to private persons, partnerships or corporations, except certain tidelands reserved solely for street purposes.
powers: may be sold to any town, city, county, city and county, municipal corporations, private persons, partnerships or corporations
limits: shall be withheld from grant or sale to private persons, partnerships, or corporations

provisions.what: All tidelands within two miles of any incorporated city, city and county, or town in this State, and fronting on the water of any harbor, estuary, bay, or inlet used for the purposes of navigation, shall be withheld from grant or sale to private persons, partnerships, or corporations
forbids: grant or sale to private persons, partnerships, or corporations
exceptions: any such tidelands, reserved to the State solely for street purposes, which the Legislature finds and declares are not used for navigation purposes and are not necessary for such purposes may be sold

provisions.what: Any such tidelands, reserved to the State solely for street purposes, which the Legislature finds and declares are not used for navigation purposes and are not necessary for such purposes may be sold to any town, city, county, city and county, municipal corporations, private persons, partnerships or corporations
conditions: which the Legislature finds and declares are not used for navigation purposes and are not necessary for such purposes
subject to such conditions as the Legislature determines are necessary to be imposed in connection with any such sales in order to protect the public interest

review.title: Public access to navigable waters
review.plain: No individual, partnership or corporation holding frontage or tidal lands on navigable water may exclude the right of way to that water when required for a public purpose, or obstruct free navigation. The Legislature shall enact laws so access stays always attainable for the people.
rights: access to the navigable waters of this State shall be always attainable for the people thereof
limits: shall be permitted to exclude the right of way to such water
nor to destroy or obstruct the free navigation of such water

provisions.what: No individual, partnership, or corporation, claiming or possessing the frontage or tidal lands of a harbor, bay, inlet, estuary, or other navigable water in this State, shall be permitted to exclude the right of way to such water whenever it is required for any public purpose, nor to destroy or obstruct the free navigation of such water
provisions.binds: No individual, partnership, or corporation, claiming or possessing the frontage or tidal lands of a harbor, bay, inlet, estuary, or other navigable water in this State
forbids: exclude the right of way to such water whenever it is required for any public purpose
destroy or obstruct the free navigation of such water

provisions.what: The Legislature shall enact such laws as will give the most liberal construction to this provision, so that access to the navigable waters of this State shall be always attainable for the people thereof
requires: enact such laws as will give the most liberal construction to this provision

review.title: Water for sale is a public use
review.plain: The use of water appropriated for sale, rental or distribution is declared a public use, subject to the regulation and control of the State in the manner prescribed by law.
powers: subject to the regulation and control of the State

provisions.what: The use of all water now appropriated, or that may hereafter be appropriated, for sale, rental, or distribution, is hereby declared to be a public use

The use of all water now appropriated, or that may hereafter be appropriated, for sale, rental, or distribution, is subject to the regulation and control of the State, in the manner to be prescribed by law
conditions: in the manner to be prescribed by law

review.title: Collecting water rates is a franchise
review.plain: The right to collect rates or compensation for water supplied to any county, city and county, or town, or their inhabitants, is a franchise and cannot be exercised except by authority of and in the manner prescribed by law.
limits: cannot be exercised except by authority of and in the manner prescribed by law

provisions.what: The right to collect rates or compensation for the use of water supplied to any county, city and county, or town, or the inhabitants thereof, is a franchise, and cannot be exercised except by authority of and in the manner prescribed by law
requires: by authority of and in the manner prescribed by law
forbids: exercising the right to collect rates or compensation for the use of water except by authority of and in the manner prescribed by law

review.title: Government land acquisitions follow state water law
review.plain: When any local, state or federal government agency acquires an interest in real property in California, accepting the interest is an agreement by the agency to conform to California laws on the acquisition, control, use and distribution of water for that land.

provisions.what: The acceptance of the interest shall constitute an agreement by the agency to conform to the laws of California as to the acquisition, control, use, and distribution of water with respect to the land so acquired
provisions.binds: Any agency of government, local, state, or federal
requires: conform to the laws of California as to the acquisition, control, use, and distribution of water with respect to the land so acquired
conditions: Whenever any agency of government, local, state, or federal, hereafter acquires any interest in real property in this State

review.title: Purpose of water protections
review.plain: The people of the State provide the guarantees and protections in this article for water rights, water quality, and fish and wildlife resources.

provisions.what: The people of the State hereby provide the following guarantees and protections in this article for water rights, water quality, and fish and wildlife resources

review.title: Changes to Senate Bill 200 water protections
review.plain: No statute changing the Senate Bill No. 200 provisions on protecting Delta fish and wildlife, existing Delta water rights, and water quality compliance takes effect unless approved by the electors, except a two-thirds legislative statute that does not reduce protection of the delta or fish and wildlife.
powers: amend or repeal, or add to, these provisions
limits: shall become effective unless approved by the electors

provisions.what: No statute amending or repealing, or adding to, the provisions of the statute enacted by Senate Bill No. 200 of the 1979–80 Regular Session of the Legislature which specify (1) the manner in which the State will protect fish and wildlife resources in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, Suisun Marsh, and San Francisco Bay system westerly of the delta; (2) the manner in which the State will protect existing water rights in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta; and (3) the manner in which the State will operate the State Water Resources Development System to comply with water quality standards and water quality control plans, shall become effective unless approved by the electors
requires: approved by the electors in the same manner as statutes amending initiative statutes are approved
exceptions: the Legislature may, by statute passed in each house by roll call vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring, amend or repeal, or add to, these provisions if the statute does not in any manner reduce the protection of the delta or fish and wildlife

provisions.what: The Legislature may, by statute, amend or repeal, or add to, these provisions
requires: statute passed in each house by roll call vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring
conditions: if the statute does not in any manner reduce the protection of the delta or fish and wildlife

review.title: No export from wild and scenic rivers
review.plain: No water from any component of the California Wild and Scenic Rivers System, as it existed on January 1, 1981, may be appropriated for export into another major hydrologic basin unless expressly authorized first by an initiative statute or a two-thirds vote of each house.
limits: No water shall be available for appropriation by storage in, or by direct diversion from, any of the components of the California Wild and Scenic Rivers System

provisions.what: No water shall be available for appropriation by storage in, or by direct diversion from, any of the components of the California Wild and Scenic Rivers System, as such system exists on January 1, 1981, where such appropriation is for export of water into another major hydrologic basin of the State
conditions: where such appropriation is for export of water into another major hydrologic basin of the State, as defined in the Department of Water Resources Bulletin 160-74
exceptions: unless such export is expressly authorized prior to such appropriation by: (a) an initiative statute approved by the electors, or (b) the Legislature, by statute passed in each house by roll call vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring

review.title: Changes to the Delta Protection Act
review.plain: No statute changing the Delta Protection Act in the Water Code takes effect unless approved by the electors, except a statute passed by two-thirds of each house that does not reduce the protection of the delta or fish and wildlife.
powers: amend or repeal, or add to, these provisions
limits: shall become effective unless approved by the electors

provisions.what: No statute amending or repealing, or adding to, the provisions of Part 4.5 (commencing with Section 12200) of Division 6 of the Water Code (the Delta Protection Act) shall become effective unless approved by the electors
requires: approved by the electors in the same manner as statutes amending initiative statutes are approved
exceptions: the Legislature may, by statute passed in each house by roll call vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring, amend or repeal, or add to, these provisions if the statute does not in any manner reduce the protection of the delta or fish and wildlife

provisions.what: The Legislature may, by statute, amend or repeal, or add to, the provisions of the Delta Protection Act
requires: statute passed in each house by roll call vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring
conditions: if the statute does not in any manner reduce the protection of the delta or fish and wildlife

review.title: No eminent domain over Delta water rights for export
review.plain: No public agency may use eminent domain to acquire Delta water rights or Delta water contract rights in order to export the water. Eminent domain may still be used to acquire land or other rights needed to build water facilities.
limits: No public agency may utilize eminent domain proceedings to acquire water rights

provisions.what: No public agency may utilize eminent domain proceedings to acquire water rights, which are held for uses within the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta as defined in Section 12220 of the Water Code, or any contract rights for water or water quality maintenance in the Delta for the purpose of exporting such water from the Delta
forbids: utilize eminent domain proceedings to acquire water rights, which are held for uses within the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, or any contract rights for water or water quality maintenance in the Delta
conditions: for the purpose of exporting such water from the Delta
exceptions: This provision shall not be construed to prohibit the utilization of eminent domain proceedings for the purpose of acquiring land or any other rights necessary for the construction of water facilities, including, but not limited to, facilities authorized in Chapter 8 (commencing with Section 12930) of Part 6 of Division 6 of the Water Code

review.title: Venue and speedy handling of water lawsuits
review.plain: Listed lawsuits over Senate Bill No. 200, the peripheral canal and related water agreements must be brought in Sacramento County within set time limits, get preference and prompt hearings, and may be transferred to the Supreme Court on any party's request.
powers: may apply to the State Board of Control for actual costs imposed by the requirements of this section upon the county
exercising the transfer authority contained in Article VI, Section 12 of the Constitution

provisions.what: The venue of any of the following actions or proceedings brought in a superior court shall be Sacramento County: (1) an action or proceeding to attack, review, set aside, void, or annul any provision of the statute enacted by Senate Bill No. 200 of the 1979–80 Regular Session; (2) to attack, review, set aside, void, or annul the determination made by the Director of Water Resources and the Director of Fish and Game pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 11255 of the Water Code; (3) which would have the effect of attacking, reviewing, preventing, or substantially delaying the construction, operation, or maintenance of the peripheral canal unit; (4) to require the State Water Resources Development System to comply with subdivision (b) of Section 11460 of the Water Code; (5) to require the Department of Water Resources or its successor agency to comply with the permanent agreement specified in subdivision (a) of Section 11256 of the Water Code; (6) to require the Department of Water Resources or its successor agency to comply with the provisions of the contracts entered into pursuant to Section 11456 of the Water Code

An action or proceeding described in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) shall be commenced within one year after the effective date of the statute enacted by Senate Bill No. 200. Any other action or proceeding described in subdivision (a) shall be commenced within one year after the cause of action arises
exceptions: unless a shorter period is otherwise provided by statute

provisions.what: The superior court or a court of appeals shall give preference to the actions or proceedings described in this section over all civil actions or proceedings pending in the court. The superior court shall commence hearing any such action or proceeding within six months after the commencement of the action or proceeding
provisions.binds: The superior court or a court of appeals
requires: give preference to the actions or proceedings described in this section over all civil actions or proceedings pending in the court
commence hearing any such action or proceeding within six months after the commencement of the action or proceeding
exceptions: any such hearing may be delayed by joint stipulation of the parties or at the discretion of the court for good cause shown

provisions.what: The provisions of this section shall supersede any provisions of law requiring courts to give preference to other civil actions or proceedings. The provisions of this subdivision may be enforced by mandamus

The Supreme Court shall, upon the request of any party, transfer to itself, before a decision in the court of appeal, any appeal or petition for extraordinary relief from an action or proceeding described in this section. The request for transfer shall receive preference on the Supreme Court’s calendar. If the action or proceeding is transferred to the Supreme Court, the Supreme Court shall commence to hear the matter within six months of the transfer
conditions: upon the request of any party
exceptions: unless the Supreme Court determines that the action or proceeding is unlikely to substantially affect (1) the construction, operation, or maintenance of the peripheral canal unit described in subdivision (a) of Section 11255 of the Water Code, (2) compliance with subdivision (b) of Section 11460 of the Water Code, (3) compliance with the permanent agreement specified in Section 11256 of the Water Code, or (4) compliance with the provisions of the contracts entered into pursuant to Section 11456 of the Water Code
unless the parties by joint stipulation request additional time or the court, for good cause shown, grants additional time

provisions.what: The remedy prescribed by the court for an action or proceeding described in paragraph (4), (5), or (6) of subdivision (a) shall include, but need not be limited to, compliance with subdivision (b) of Section 11460 of the Water Code, the permanent agreement specified in Section 11256 of the Water Code, or the provisions of the contracts entered into pursuant to Section 11456 of the Water Code
The Board of Supervisors of the County of Sacramento may apply to the State Board of Control for actual costs imposed by the requirements of this section upon the county
provisions.holder: The Board of Supervisors of the County of Sacramento

provisions.what: The State Board of Control shall pay such actual costs
Nothing in this Article shall be construed as prohibiting the Supreme Court from exercising the transfer authority contained in Article VI, Section 12 of the Constitution
conditions: Notwithstanding the provisions of this section

review.title: State agencies must honor water protections
review.plain: State agencies shall exercise their authorized powers in a manner consistent with the protections provided by this article.

provisions.what: State agencies shall exercise their authorized powers in a manner consistent with the protections provided by this article
requires: exercise their authorized powers in a manner consistent with the protections provided by this article

review.title: Article depends on Senate Bill 200
review.plain: This article has no force or effect unless Senate Bill No. 200 of the 1979–80 Regular Session of the Legislature is enacted and takes effect.

provisions.what: This article shall have no force or effect unless Senate Bill No. 200 of the 1979–80 Regular Session of the Legislature is enacted and takes effect
conditions: unless Senate Bill No. 200 of the 1979–80 Regular Session of the Legislature is enacted and takes effect

review.title: Name of the article
review.plain: This article may be cited as the Marine Resources Protection Act of 1990.

provisions.what: This article shall be known and may be cited as the Marine Resources Protection Act of 1990

review.title: Definitions for marine resources protection
review.plain: Defines "District", "Ocean waters" and the Marine Resources Protection "Zone" (waters around the Channel Islands and near the southern mainland coast), and says Fish and Game Code references mean the statutes in effect on January 1, 1990.

provisions.what: “District” means a fish and game district as defined in the Fish and Game Code by statute on January 1, 1990
terms: "District": a fish and game district as defined in the Fish and Game Code by statute on January 1, 1990

provisions.what: All references to Fish and Game Code sections, articles, chapters, parts, and divisions are defined as those statutes in effect on January 1, 1990
exceptions: Except as specifically provided in this article

provisions.what: “Ocean waters” means the waters of the Pacific Ocean regulated by the State
terms: "Ocean waters": the waters of the Pacific Ocean regulated by the State

provisions.what: “Zone” means the Marine Resources Protection zone established pursuant to this article, consisting of: (1) waters less than 70 fathoms or within one mile, whichever is less, around the Channel Islands of San Miguel, Santa Rosa, Santa Cruz, Anacapa, San Nicolaus, Santa Barbara, Santa Catalina, and San Clemente; (2) the area within three nautical miles offshore of the mainland coast, and within three nautical miles off any manmade breakwater, between a line extending due west from Point Arguello and a line extending due west from the Mexican border; (3) waters less than 35 fathoms between a line running 180 degrees true from Point Fermin and a line running 270 degrees true from the south jetty of Newport Harbor
terms: "Zone": the Marine Resources Protection zone established pursuant to this article, consisting of the waters around the Channel Islands, the area off the mainland coast between Point Arguello and the Mexican border, and the waters between Point Fermin and Newport Harbor described in paragraphs (1) to (3)

review.title: Gill and trammel nets banned in the zone
review.plain: From 1991 through 1993, gill nets or trammel nets may be used in the zone only under a nontransferable Department of Fish and Game permit. On and after January 1, 1994, they shall not be used in the zone.
limits: may only be used in the zone pursuant to a nontransferable permit
shall not be used in the zone

provisions.what: From January 1, 1991, to December 31, 1993, inclusive, gill nets or trammel nets may only be used in the zone pursuant to a nontransferable permit issued by the Department of Fish and Game pursuant to Section 5
requires: a nontransferable permit issued by the Department of Fish and Game pursuant to Section 5

provisions.what: On and after January 1, 1994, gill nets and trammel nets shall not be used in the zone
forbids: using gill nets and trammel nets in the zone

review.title: Gill net limits for rockfish and northern waters
review.plain: Gill and trammel nets may not be used to take any rockfish. North of Point Arguello, their use is governed by the Fish and Game Code provisions in effect in 1990 or 1989. The Legislature may add restrictions; the Director may not authorize use where it is not permitted.
powers: imposing more restrictions on the use and/or possession of gill nets or trammel nets
limits: may not be used to take any species of rockfish
shall not authorize the use of gill nets or trammel nets in any area where the use is not permitted

provisions.what: Gill nets and trammel nets may not be used to take any species of rockfish
forbids: using gill nets and trammel nets to take any species of rockfish
conditions: Notwithstanding any other provision of law

provisions.what: In ocean waters north of Point Arguello on and after the effective date of this article, the use of gill nets and trammel nets shall be regulated by the provisions of Article 4, Article 5 and Article 6 of Chapter 3 of Part 3 of Division 6 of the Fish and Game Code, or any regulation or order issued pursuant to these articles, in effect on January 1, 1990
exceptions: as to Sections 8680, 8681, 8681.7, and 8682, and subdivisions (a) through (f), inclusive of Section 8681.5 of the Fish and Game Code, or any regulation or order issued pursuant to these sections, the provisions in effect on January 1, 1989, shall control where not in conflict with other provisions of this article, and shall be applicable to all ocean waters

provisions.what: The Legislature shall not be precluded from imposing more restrictions on the use and/or possession of gill nets or trammel nets
conditions: Notwithstanding the provisions of this section

provisions.what: The Director of the Department of Fish and Game shall not authorize the use of gill nets or trammel nets in any area where the use is not permitted even if the director makes specified findings
provisions.binds: The Director of the Department of Fish and Game
forbids: authorize the use of gill nets or trammel nets in any area where the use is not permitted

review.title: Gill net permits during the phase-out
review.plain: For 1991 through 1993, the Department of Fish and Game shall issue a gill net or trammel net permit for the zone to any applicant with a commercial fishing license and a Section 8681 permit who owns or operates a vessel equipped with such a net.

provisions.what: The Department of Fish and Game shall issue a permit to use a gill net or trammel net in the zone for the period specified in subdivision (a) of Section 3 to any applicant who meets both of the following requirements
provisions.binds: The Department of Fish and Game
requires: (a) Has a commercial fishing license issued pursuant to Sections 7850–7852.3 of the Fish and Game Code
(b) Has a permit issued pursuant to Section 8681 of the Fish and Game Code and is presently the owner or operator of a vessel equipped with a gill net or trammel net

review.title: Gill net permit fees
review.plain: The Department of Fish and Game shall charge fees for Section 5 permits of $250 in 1991, 500 in 1992, and 1,000 in 1993.

provisions.what: The Department of Fish and Game shall charge the following fees for permits issued pursuant to Section 5: 1991, $250; 1992, 500; 1993, 1,000
provisions.binds: The Department of Fish and Game

review.title: Compensation for giving up gill net permits
review.plain: Permit holders who timely notified the Department of Fish and Game could surrender their permits and stop gill or trammel net fishing in the zone for a one time compensation based on past landings, subject to verification, appeal, and enabling legislation by July 1, 1993.
rights: may appeal that decision to the Fish and Game Commission
limits: shall not be compensated pursuant to subdivision (b)
no compensation shall be paid under this article

provisions.what: Within 90 days after the effective date of this section, every person who intends to seek the compensation provided in subdivision (b) shall notify the Department of Fish and Game, on forms provided by the department, of that intent
provisions.binds: Every person who intends to seek the compensation provided in subdivision (b)

provisions.what: Any person who does not submit the form within that 90-day period shall not be compensated pursuant to subdivision (b)
conditions: does not submit the form within that 90-day period

provisions.what: The department shall publish a list of all persons submitting the form within 120 days after the effective date of this section
provisions.binds: The Department of Fish and Game

provisions.what: Any person who holds a permit issued pursuant to Section 5 and operates in the zone may surrender that permit to the department and agree to permanently discontinue fishing with gill or trammel nets in the zone, for which he or she shall receive a one time compensation which shall be based upon the average annual ex vessel value of the fish other than any species of rockfish landed by a fisherman, taken pursuant to a valid general gill net or trammel net permit within the zone during the years 1983 to 1987, inclusive
provisions.holder: Any person who holds a permit issued pursuant to Section 5 and operates in the zone
requires: surrender that permit to the department
agree to permanently discontinue fishing with gill or trammel nets in the zone

provisions.what: The department shall verify those landings by reviewing logs and landing receipts submitted to it
provisions.binds: The Department of Fish and Game

provisions.what: Any person who is denied compensation by the department as a result of the department’s failure to verify landings may appeal that decision to the Fish and Game Commission
provisions.holder: Any person who is denied compensation by the department as a result of the department’s failure to verify landings

provisions.what: The State Board of Control shall, prior to the disbursement of any funds, verify the eligibility of each person seeking compensation and the amount of the compensation to be provided in order to ensure compliance with this section
No compensation shall be paid under this article
conditions: Unless the Legislature enacts any required enabling legislation to implement this section on or before July 1, 1993
